claims.text: Role in ED: second-line: VED, self-injected intracavernosal injections or intraurethral PGE1;
claims.quote: Vacuum erection device or self-administered intracavernosal injections (ICI) or intraurethral prostaglandin E1 (second-line treatment)

claims.text: self-administered intraurethral or intracavernosal alprostadil gives erections lasting a mean 30 to 60 min;
claims.quote: Alprostadil (prostaglandin E1), self-administered via intraurethral insertion or intracavernosal injection, can produce erections with a mean duration of 30 to 60 minutes.

claims.text: intracavernous alprostadil may be compounded w papaverine and phentolamine;
claims.quote: Intracavernous alprostadil may be compounded with papaverine and phentolamine for increased efficacy when necessary.

claims.text: intraurethral is less effective than injection; adding it to a PDE5 inhibitor may help pts who fail a PDE5 inhibitor alone.
claims.quote: Intraurethral therapy is less effective at producing satisfactory erection than intracavernosal injection. Combination therapy with a PDE5 inhibitor and intraurethral alprostadil may be useful for some patients who fail to respond to oral PDE5 inhibitors alone.

claims.text: Caverject label: Alprostadil (Caverject) intracavernosal dose (vasculogenic, psychogenic or mixed ED): start 2.5 mcg;
claims.quote: Initiate dosing with 2.5 mcg of CAVERJECT intracavernosally

claims.text: partial response: another 2.5 mcg w.in 1 h (new vial each dose);
claims.quote: If there is a partial response at 2.5 mcg, administer another dose of 2.5 mcg within 1 hour. Use a new vial for each dose of CAVERJECT.
During titration, no more than 2 doses should be given within a 24-hour period.

claims.text: further titration in 5 to 10 mcg steps ≥ 24 h apart;
claims.quote: If additional titration is required, administer doses in increments of 5 to 10 mcg at least 24 hours apart.

claims.text: target: an erection suitable for intercourse lasting ≤ 1 h;
claims.quote: The optimal dose should produce an erection suitable for intercourse that does not exceed a duration of 1 hour.
Doses greater than 60 mcg are not recommended.

claims.text: Home use: ≤ 3 times weekly, ≥ 24 h between doses.
claims.quote: The recommended frequency of injection is no more than 3 times weekly, with at least 24 hours between each dose.
claims.locator: 2.2 Recommended Dosage for Erectile Dysfunction › Maintenance Dosage for Patient Home Use

claims.text: CI: conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell anemia or trait, multiple myeloma, leukemia);
claims.quote: Men who have conditions that predispose them to priapism, such as sickle cell anemia or sickle cell trait, multiple myeloma, or leukemia

claims.text: fibrotic conditions of the penis (angulation, cavernosal fibrosis, Peyronie dz);
claims.quote: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in men with fibrotic conditions of the penis, such as anatomical deformation, angulation, cavernosal fibrosis, or Peyronie's disease

claims.text: Erection > 4 h: seek immediate medical help (untreated priapism → tissue damage, permanent loss of potency).
claims.quote: In the event of an erection that persists longer than 4 hours, the patient should seek immediate medical assistance. If priapism is not treated immediately, penile tissue damage and permanent loss of potency may result.

claims.text: Penile fibrosis (3% overall; 7.8% in an up-to-18-month self-injection study): examine the penis periodically; stop if angulation or cavernosal fibrosis develops.
claims.quote: The overall incidence of penile fibrosis reported in clinical studies with CAVERJECT was 3%. In one self-injection clinical study where duration of use was up to 18 months, the incidence of penile fibrosis was 7.8%. Physical examination of the penis should be performed periodically, to detect signs of penile fibrosis. Treatment with CAVERJECT should be discontinued in patients who develop penile angulation or cavernosal fibrosis.

claims.text: Can cause hypotension: ⍉ in known cavernosal venous leakage.
claims.quote: Intracavernous injections of CAVERJECT can increase peripheral blood levels of alprostadil which can result in hypotension. Avoid use of CAVERJECT in patients with known cavernosal venous leakage.

claims.text: Anticoagulants (warfarin, heparin): injection-site bleeding; compress the site for 5 min.
claims.quote: Patients on anticoagulants, such as warfarin or heparin, may have increased propensity for injection site bleeding after intracavernosal injection with CAVERJECT. Compress the site of injection with an alcohol swab or sterile gauze for 5 minutes.
claims.locator: 5.4 Injection Site Bleeding When Used with Anticoagulants

claims.text: Combos w other intracavernosal vasoactive agents: safety and efficacy not established; ↑ risk of prolonged erection, priapism and hypotension.
claims.quote: The safety and efficacy of combinations of CAVERJECT and other vasoactive agents injected intracavernosally have not been established in clinical studies. The risks of prolonged erection, priapism, and hypotension may be increased.
claims.locator: 5.6 Risks of Use in Combination with Other Vasoactive Medications Injected Intracavernosally
